summary:
plan.md fixes the west Tunnel Tops on the mapped terrain (2x2 blocks per map cell). On the low flat sit the Outpost (a log Fort with a deck 8 up, log piles, a runnel) and a meadow; the Cliff Walk with two timber overlooks runs along the bluff top (z 44..58, where the map actually rises 3→7, not the brief's z 4..20; the brief's meadow at x 1..50 is paved W on the map, so the meadow is moved into the park).
Further south come the mounded Big Lawn and a smooth_stone two-bore portal at x 41 swallowing the Parkway (z 80..91). Calcite-and-spruce seating tiers and a promenade face north along the high south edge.
It reads as this park, not a generic lawn, through curving pale smooth_sandstone paths, grey-green, ochre and purple native drifts, wind-shorn flat-topped cypress groves, slim dark lamp posts, and four path crossings fixed at x 119 for the east half. West half of Tunnel Tops on the mapped terrain: pale curving smooth_sandstone paths, mounded Big Lawn, Outpost log Fort and play ground, Cliff Walk with two timber overlooks, calcite-and-spruce seating terraces and promenade, and a smooth_stone two-bore portal for the Parkway.
Native drifts (azalea mounds, grasses, allium/cornflower, dead bush) and wind-shorn dark cypress/pine groves fill the rest, lit by dark lamp posts and hidden light under moss carpet.
Six parts: terrain, portal, outpost, terraces, planting, lighting. No interior rooms.

Terrain and paving: parts/terrain.mjs plus heights-data.mjs and sitemap.txt: whole-box ground heights (heights.json), water, W-cell walks, roads with markings, parking with stall lines, parkway at y4 with median and bore floor, smooth_sandstone paths with slab half-steps, and the Big Lawn mound. make.sh runs clean (no refused writes or off-palette blocks) and the render reads right.
Tunnel columns (x41..42 z76..95, x43..50 z79..92) are left hollow at y4 so the portal part can build into air.
polish: P2 must fill the earth bank and lid over x43..50 z76..78 and build the tunnel walls, ceiling and soil into the hollow columns (x41..42 z76..95, x43..50 z79..92). The ground is left hollow there at height 4.
build.mjs reads heights.json before the parts run, so heights.json must exist. It is written now, and `node -e` with heights-data.mjs regenerates it.
The west-bank path stops at (43,97) and does not reach the Parkway walk at (40,95), because the cut is hollow there.
The parkway ramp slabs and the cliff-walk descent along the west bluff are approximate.
Elements.md ticks not done individually. Elements 1-6 are built; 10 (lid cover) is left to P2/P5.

waste.what: Wrote my own cell-painting road/marking and 4-connected path-sweep code, instead of using roadStrip and curvePath. Those helpers assume one fixed y and a flat surface, and the real ground varies.
waste.cost: about 80 lines of local code
waste.tool: A height-aware curvePath(points, width, heightFn) with automatic half-step slabs, and a roadStrip that follows a height function

waste.what: Worked out by hand that build.mjs reads heights.json before any part runs. That meant a separate generator step and a heights-data.mjs module shared by build.mjs and the part.
waste.cost: one design detour
waste.tool: build.mjs should call a heights generator itself, or the plan should name a pre-step; the site map should ship as a data file (sitemap.txt) next to the height map

companions.task: Lay the Parkway ramps and cut slopes with proper grades, and put the lane markings through the portal.
Build the parkway kerbs and the pond kerb in smooth stone with slab edges.

summary:
Tunnel portal and cut: Tunnel portal and cut (P2) built in parts/portal.mjs: calcite-coped portal face with two mouths and a pier lantern, two bores (sea lanterns at y8, black back wall, slab ceiling at y9), a lid of soil, slab ceiling and grass at y10 over x43..53 z76..95, and stepped cut walls (y9/8/7) with grass-topped earth banks.
make.sh runs whole: the portal line reads 1402 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. render tiles and a west zoom read as a portal under a grass lid.
plan.md checklist ticked for P2, elements 7-10 marked built, and a P2 note added to Notes.
polish: `$MCD check` reports 6 'unsupported' sea_lantern blocks at y8 (x43/46/49, z82 and z89). The ceiling is the spec's bottom slab at y9, and the lanterns are full blocks, so this looks like a false positive. A full-stone ceiling did not clear it either, so I reverted to the spec slab; the check needs a rule for full-block lights.
The lid's east edge (x52..53) stands 2 blocks above the mapped y8 ground, so there is a raw 2-block step at the lid's east side. P4/P5 should soften it with slabs or stairs.
The cut walls step down in 3 segments and the earth banks step with them, but the steps between segments are raw 1-block steps with no slab softening.
The lid path (elements.md item 10) is P1's paint, not built here; the planting over the lid (grass at y10) is for P5.

waste.what: Lid soil, slab ceiling and grass at y10 were filled cell by cell with nested loops, plus the bank dirt and grass at each cut-wall step.
waste.cost: about 1,400 blocks placed by loops; 4 bank and lid passes written by hand, plus the sea-lantern ceiling experiment and its revert
waste.tool: A vocab helper such as lidCover(g, x0,z0,x1,z1,{ soilTo, ceilingY, grassY, skip }) and earthBank(g, x0,x1,z0,z1,hTop) would replace the hand loops. A check that tells a full-block light from a hanging lantern would have settled the sea-lantern question in one run.

waste.what: Checking the sea-lantern warning by re-running make and check after each change, to learn which ceiling clears it.
waste.cost: 3 make+check cycles, about 1 minute
waste.tool: `$MCD check` could explain the rule it applied to sea_lantern (hanging-type or full-block), so a builder can tell a real fault from a false positive without trial and error.

companions.task: Lay the cut's retaining walls and their steps down westward, and the earth banks behind them, grass-topped at each course, with the slab softening between steps.
Confirm that the sea lanterns at y8 in the bores and the pier lantern at (40,7,85) are the only lights inside the tunnel, and check the bore's dark cells.

summary:
Outpost play area: Outpost play area built in parts/outpost.mjs (1333 blocks, no refused writes, no off-palette): Fort lookout on a raised footprint with rope net, climbing log pile, five crisscrossed balance logs, sand pit and play-ground patches, 8 rim boulders, the z38 water runnel across x119, the lowFence lines with gates, and three picnic tables.
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt; mcd check shows 0 floating blocks, 6 orphan warnings on the picnic-table top slabs. Fort, runnel and balance logs checked in zoom renders.
Element 18 (meadow drifts and mown loop) is not built here; it belongs to P3/P5 planting. Plan.md checklist ticked and a P3 note appended.
polish: Element 18 (meadow): the mown 2-wide grass_block loop and the tall-grass/cornflower drifts were not built here. Planting (P5) must leave the loop unplanted.
Fort footprint raised one block to grass at y4 on the cells where the ground is 3, so the tower stands on a 1-block plinth with a raw step at its edge. The plan asks for slab softening; not done.
Fort entry is one cell wide (x83 z28 y4..6), not the planned 82..83, because the ladder at x82 needs planks behind it.
Log pile sits at y5..9 (surface 4 plus one), not the planned 4..8.
Runnel channel is cut to y3 at x94..99 z36..40, where the mound rises to 4; that is a 1-block cut into the lawn with no slab softening.
Picnic-table top slabs are unsupported by design (picnicTable helper), so check reports 6 orphan warnings. Visually acceptable in the render.
Fence lines follow the ground in runs of equal height: x68..117 at z19 and z43 and z68 at x68; the z43 gates are three cells wide at x90..92.

waste.what: Worked out the surface height under every structure by hand: printed heights.json slices with node one-liners for the fort, runnel and picnic tables, then picked y values per helper.
waste.cost: about 4 node probes and 3 wrong guesses at y (fort y=3 vs 4, log pile y4 vs y5, runnel H=4 cells)
waste.tool: A helper that takes a footprint and returns the surface y per cell and the max/min, or a mode where each vocab helper takes the surface and places from surface+1 by itself, so y conventions are not guessed.

waste.what: Fort roof and apex: floating apex slabs and planks found only by running make.sh and check, then support columns added by trial (y14, then y15, then y13..15). Three rebuild cycles.
waste.cost: 3 build+check cycles, about 6 minutes
waste.tool: fortTower should lay its own support column from the deck to the apex and document its y convention (surface vs first air). check --json should name the support cell to add.

waste.what: Ladder backing: the entry opening and the ladder's back wall are in conflict (the ladder bottom at y4..5 has nothing behind it). Fixed by hand with planks.
waste.cost: 1 retry plus a check pass
waste.tool: fortTower option for entry width, with the ladder backing generated from the same entry cells.

waste.what: Fence lines that cross ground of changing height: I split them into equal-height runs by hand (fenceLine) and called lowFence per run.
waste.cost: about 40 lines of run-splitting code
waste.tool: lowFence (or a new fenceFollow) that places each post at its own ground +1 and steps the rail, so the caller does not split runs.

waste.what: Water runnel where the ground rises above the channel: carved the cells above the channel by hand.
waste.cost: one carve loop, one check
waste.tool: runnel option to cut its channel to the ground (carve the cells above it where H is higher) instead of the caller doing it.

waste.what: make.sh once failed on a mktemp name collision (File exists), which needed a re-run.
waste.cost: 1 extra make.sh run
waste.tool: make.sh should retry mktemp, or use a unique suffix (e.g. $$).

companions.task: The Fort: posts, deck, the ladder and its back wall, and the entry, so the single-cell opening and the ladder's backing are settled before any of it is placed.
The Fort hip cap and the apex support column, so the roof ring and its supports come out right on the first pass.
The runnel's gradient and the channel cut through the rising ground at x94..99, so the water and the stone walls sit at one level.
The rope net, the climbing log pile and the balance logs, so their anchor points and climb heights are right for children, not just for the view.

summary:
Overlooks, terraces and promenade: parts/terraces.mjs builds the Cliff Walk rail on z57, two timber overlook decks (x74..81, x100..107 z50..56) with benches and lamps, and graded seating terraces on both banks (west x57..77, east x100..115, z89..102) with aisles and seat walls.
Also the freestanding seat walls at z85, a light paving promenade z104..107 with calcite edges, six benches facing north, and planter troughs on z103.
make.sh ran clean: P4 placed 1401 blocks, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. mcd check reports no floating or unsupported blocks, and fit is OK. Zoom renders of the terraces and decks read as the planned features.
polish: West terrace narrowed to x57..77 (plan said 52..77) so the lid path at x53..56 keeps running through it; the lid path is P1's, so the terrace could not take that strip without cutting it.
East bank planter at x116..119 not built (plan calls for one).
Cliff Walk rail is at ground+1 per column (y7 or y8) instead of a flat y8, because the bluff ground at z57 is 6 to 7 and a flat y8 would float over the 6s.
Terraces were checked only in one close zoom render; the seat-wall facing on tier 1 and 2 north edges was not judged at street scale.
Freestanding seat walls use over:true so the calcite replaces the grass at y8 where the ground is 8.

waste.what: Terrace grading cell by cell: working out which ground to cut above each tier surface and what to fill under it, column by column, with a hand-written carve loop
waste.cost: about 3 tries and a few hundred cells computed by hand against heights.json
waste.tool: A grade(x0,z0,x1,z1,y,{clear,fill}) helper in vocab/h3 that cuts grass/dirt above a surface and fills below, returning refusals, so a terrace is one call

waste.what: Checking ground heights in my zones by printing rows of heights.json with ad hoc node one-liners
waste.cost: 4 probe commands before the first build
waste.tool: mcd heights <x0,z0,x1,z1> (prints the surface height grid for a box, with P1's paths and water marked)

waste.what: Finding out which P1 path cells sit inside my promenade and terrace boxes by reading terrain.mjs by eye
waste.cost: one full read of terrain.mjs and a guess at the path footprints
waste.tool: A conflict report from runParts for earlier parts' cells inside a part's footprint, before the part is written (currently only refusals after the fact)

waste.what: Writing a custom cliff rail and promenade loop because the vocab cliffRail and promenade helpers take one y and refuse occupied cells
waste.cost: about 40 lines of hand code and 2 retries
waste.tool: vocab helpers that accept a height function (y = (x,z) => H+1) and a skip-occupied mode, not just air-only writes

waste.what: Eyeballing the renders at small size to judge seat walls and terraces
waste.cost: 2 zoom renders, judged by eye
waste.tool: mcd zoom --tiles with a labelled grid of block coordinates, so a tier's z-row and y can be read off the picture

companions.task: Build the calcite seat walls and terrace risers, and cut the tier steps and half-steps in the aisles, so the riser lines and edge courses are worked stone, not single blocks.
Frame the overlook decks, benches and rail: posts, planks, the open trapdoor arms and the spruce fence joins, checking the rail heights where the bluff ground changes.
Plant the promenade planter troughs and the grass at the terrace edges, and choose the grass and dirt patches around the terraces so the planting drifts meet the paving cleanly.

summary:
Planting and trees: parts/planting.mjs builds the planting: 10 azalea shrub heaps on the north and west bluffs, 28 cypress and pine trees in the plan's groves (lid, SW edge, south, SE, NW meadow), and grey-green, ochre, purple and meadow drifts on every planted soil cell, with podzol and moss patches. The mown loop, Big Lawn, terraces, decks and pads stay clear.
make.sh finished and saved a whole build.nbt; this part logged no refused writes and no off-palette blocks. $MCD check shows 0 floating or unsupported blocks. The front-left and street renders show the groves and drifts reading as planting.
Plan.md's P5 checkbox is ticked and a P5 note added; elements.md has no checkbox column, so its rows 18, 25 and 26 are built but not marked there.
polish: Only 10 shrub heaps; the plan's bluff scrub is denser. The flat-footprint rule for the sloped bluffs rejected most candidates, and mounds are not built on slopes.
No sunflower clumps (sunflower is not among the drift kinds) and no rooted_dirt or coarse_dirt patches in the beds.
The south grove x60..75 z108..135 is mostly under the B pad x66..79 z112..133, so it holds fewer trees than planned.
Lid planting is the generic drift and grove pass over the lid soil; I did not verify lid trees individually in the render.
elements.md has no checkbox column, so rows 18, 25 and 26 are built but not ticked there.
Other parts were still stubs when this ran, so the render shows planting over bare terrain and the bluffs and overlooks are not yet built around it.

waste.what: Tree placement was a seeded trial-and-error loop: random spots, spacing checks and a refusal retry until each grove's count was met.
waste.cost: about 800 candidate tries per tree across 28 trees, with no per-grove count or spacing feedback from the toolkit
waste.tool: a placeGrove or scatter helper in vocab (grove box, species mix, min spacing, soil-only test) would replace my loop

waste.what: Surface lookup: I scanned each column down from y 29 for its top soil block, because the planting must sit on what the earlier parts laid (lid at y10, paths, roads).
waste.cost: about 17k columns times up to 29 blockAt calls per pass, run twice
waste.tool: a build-library helper like topSolid(g, x, z) or a surface map written by the terrain part would save the scan

waste.what: Shrub heaps on sloped bluffs: I searched candidate centres for footprints that sit on one flat soil level, then tuned the size and spacing by hand after a first run gave only 4 heaps.
waste.cost: two builds and about 20k sampled footprints
waste.tool: shrubMound with an optional per-column surface (or a sloped mode that steps the base) would avoid the flat-only search

waste.what: Per-cell drift calls, because drift() takes a single y for its whole box and the bluffs and lid change level.
waste.cost: about 17k single-cell calls, each creating its own writer
waste.tool: drift accepting a surface function (x, z) => y, or a heights-aware variant, would make one call per bed

waste.what: Sitemap character lookup for exclusions (park, road, B pad), read from a copied sitemap.txt, plus my own keep-clear boxes listed by hand.
waste.cost: hand-written boxes for the lawn, play area, terraces, decks and pads
waste.tool: a site-zone lookup in vocab (site letter and the plan's zone table) would replace the hand-copied keep-clear list

companions.task: Place the cypress and pine groves by species: crown width, lean and spacing, and which trees sit over the lid and which on the bluff edge, so the groves read as the Presidio's windswept stands.
Lay the podzol and moss patches and the drift clumps by hand, so the bed ground and plant mix look like the native scrub rather than a random scatter.
Plant the north and west bluff scrub on the slope, stepping each shrub heap down the bank, so the bluff reads as coastal scrub, not a row of flat mounds.

polish: mcd light reports dark cells around the placed hidden lights on the parking lot (x 0..19, z 36..42 at feet y 4) even though the light blocks are at level 15 in the saved NBT. Not resolved: the tool may not count `light` blocks as sources, or the feet level is off. Verify with `mcd light` against a build that has the planting part in it.

Only the terrain part's paths are in this copy; the other parts are stubs here, so the lamp count (88) and hidden-light count (88) will change at the final merge. The lighting part reads the final grid, so it must run last.

Fort, overlook deck and terrace lamps are NOT placed by this part: overlookDeck (P4) places its own two lamp posts, and fortTower (P3) its hanging lanterns. Check at merge that every deck has its two posts.
Lamp spacing is Euclidean 9 along the BFS order of each path, so forks and path ends get a lamp only where the spacing allows; there is no explicit fork pass.
Render at --front n is too small to judge the lamp placement by eye; street.png shows the posts only as dark verticals. A close-up zoom at the outpost path and the Cliff Walk is still needed.

waste.what: Checking the light map by reading text rows and counting zeros per row with awk, because `mcd light` prints a whole 120-wide site map and has no per-cell or per-region summary.
waste.cost: about 6 full map dumps and 3 tool calls; no per-cell conclusion reached on the parking-lot dark cells
waste.tool: `mcd light --box x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1 --json` returning dark cells as a list, plus a per-light reach report (which hidden light lights which cells).

waste.what: Hand-written column scan for the top block and path/ground classification (a 120x146 top-block map built cell by cell in the part).
waste.cost: about 17k columns x 30 blockAt calls per run, about 1 s each build; a helper was written here that others will need
waste.tool: A shared surfaceMap(g) helper in vocab (top y, top block, path flag per column) so parts stop rescanning the grid.

waste.what: Picking lamp spots: a greedy spacing of 9 blocks along a BFS of path cells, with the side check written by hand.
waste.cost: one generator (parts/lighting.mjs), 3 rebuilds to fix moss_carpet floating over air and light coverage on gray_concrete
waste.tool: vocab helper placeLampsAlongPaths(g, {spacing, sideOf}) that also returns refused spots; and a check that carpet and other decor sit on a same-level support, so decor never floats.

companions.task: Check the light map against the finished planting: confirm that the hidden lights really light the parking lot and the bioswale islands, and say which dark cells are real.

Decide where the lamp posts go on the outpost and meadow paths and whether the Cliff Walk overlooks need lamps beyond the deck posts, so the posts stay beside the paths and not in the planting drifts.

summary:
inspection: Fit: all 220 'grass on bottom slab' issues fixed. The lid ceiling (portal.mjs) and bore ceilings (vocab/h1.mjs tunnelBore) are now full smooth_stone blocks.
Walk: unchanged, still ok (17455 cells reached, no rooms). make.sh rebuilt build.nbt.
Fit now reports OK.

waste.what: Traced each 'grass_block on a bottom slab' cell back to the slab that placed it. The fit message names only the cell, so the source had to be found by grepping for slab calls and reading portal.mjs.
waste.cost: 3 tool calls, plus one extra rebuild and check cycle
waste.tool: fit should name the block under the flagged cell and the part or helper that wrote it (here: smooth_stone_slab bottom at y 9, from tunnelBore).

waste.what: The first fix cleared only the lid footprint (220 cells). The bore ceilings under the same grass (112 more cells) only appeared on the re-check, because the message groups by cell with no count per source.
waste.cost: 1 extra make.sh and fit cycle
waste.tool: fit output could group issues by source block/helper and print a count per group, so a shared cause shows in one pass.
